title: Lapland: where lung cancer care falls behind, and what EUR 1 million a year should buy first
markdown:
# Lapland: where lung cancer care falls behind, and what EUR 1 million a year should buy first

## The gap in one sentence
Lapland had the highest lung cancer death rate among residents aged 65+ of all 23 counties in 2021–2025: 227.0 per 100,000, against 178.6 nationally (measured) [^statfin_13u5]. Only 18.5% of lung cancer patients got curative-intent treatment in 2019–2023, against 27.0% nationally, the lowest of 22 counties (measured) [^fcr_lung_quality_report]. At the top-quartile county rate, about 16.8 more patients a year would get curative-intent treatment; this is arithmetic on registry shares, not a causal estimate [^fcr_lung_quality_report]. The model estimates 155 days (142–168) from first symptom to treatment start [^model].

## Where the days are lost
The step furthest above the national value is first symptom to first primary care contact, estimated at 63 days (53–74) against 56 nationally [^model]. The drivers listed for this step include 11.4% daily smokers against 9.1% nationally [^sotkanet_4404] and 28.6% of residents in sparsely populated rural areas against 4.4% [^statfin_11ra]. Diagnosis to treatment start is measured at 29.6 days for the Northern Finland (OYS) collaborative area, weighted by Lapland's treatment mix, against 36.9 nationally (1.1.2018–30.6.2022) [^src_fi_assets_files_2024_12_Keuhkosyopa_Suomessa_pdf_p28].

## Three actions
1. **What:** Low-dose CT screening with smoking-cessation support for 50–74-year-old long-term heavy smokers [^model]. This needs a national decision, because a county cannot start screening alone [^model]. **Owner:** Ministry of Social Affairs and Health and Palko (decision), Finnish Cancer Registry (steering), county (delivery). **Cost:** EUR 548,645 a year (assumption) [^model]. **Expected effect:** 0 days saved, 4.38 (3.21–5.56) deaths avoided per year (estimated), with benefits arriving after years [^model]. **Evidence:** [^ev_ldct_screening_1] [^ev_ldct_screening_2] [^ev_ldct_screening_3] [^ev_ldct_screening_4]. **Roadmap:** 2.3.4, Establish new national screening programmes [^roadmap_2.3.4].
2. **What:** Cessation medication and counselling for every current smoker at the first specialist visit [^model]. **Owner:** Chief physician and head nurse of pulmonology. **Cost:** EUR 57,800 a year (assumption) [^model]. **Expected effect:** 0 days saved, 0.45 (0.31–0.58) deaths avoided per year (estimated) [^model]. **Evidence:** [^ev_smoking_cessation_at_diagnosis_1] (observational). **Roadmap:** 3.1.2, Cancer-specific care pathway descriptions [^roadmap_3.1.2].
3. **What:** Primary-care chest X-rays reported while the patient waits, with CT within days if the X-ray is suspicious [^model]. **Owner:** Chief radiologist with the chief physician of primary care. **Cost:** EUR 109,000 a year (assumption) [^model]. **Expected effect:** 23 days (11–29) saved and 0.3 (−0.05 to 0.76) deaths avoided per year (estimated); no benefit cannot be ruled out [^model]. **Evidence:** [^ev_same_day_cxr_ct_1]. **Roadmap:** 2.5.2, Standard referral criteria for quick transfer to specialist care [^roadmap_2.5.2].

## What to measure from Monday
- Date of first symptom and of first primary care contact for every lung cancer patient.
- Days from referral to first pulmonology visit for suspected lung cancer.
- Days from first specialist visit to diagnosis, and from diagnosis to treatment start, for the county.
- Stage at diagnosis for every lung cancer patient.

## Limits of this analysis
The step days are county-level estimates built from assumed priors, not measurements of individual pathways [^model]. As a check, not a validation, the estimated clock correlated with none of three measured outcomes beyond chance (curative intent rho −0.30, p 0.17) [^model]. The national total of 155 days was reported by Yle in 2026 from an unpublished four-city Finnish study [^src_yle_fi_a_74_20250979].
